bookInfo.name: New History of the Five Dynasties

title.zh: 卷五十 雜傳第三十八: 王峻 王殷 劉詞 王環 折從阮
title.en: Volume 50 Miscellaneous Biographies 30: Wang Jun, Wang Yin, Liu Ci, Wang Huan, Zhe Congruan
title.raw: 卷五十 雜傳第三十八: 王峻 王殷 劉詞 王環 折從阮 Volume 50 Miscellaneous Biographies 30: Wang Jun, Wang Yin, Liu Ci, Wang Huan, Zhe Congruan

sentences.zh: 周太祖鎮天雄軍，峻為監軍。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu held the Tianxiong army, Jun was its supervising commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhou Taizu held Tianxiong, Jun served as supervising commissioner.

sentences.zh: 漢隱帝已殺大臣史弘肇等，又遣人殺周太祖及峻等，峻等遂與太祖舉兵犯京師。

translations.literal: Han’s Hidden Emperor had already killed the great ministers Shi Hongzhao and others, and also sent men to kill Zhou Taizu and Jun and the rest; Jun and the others then joined Taizu in raising troops to strike the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Hidden Emperor had killed Shi Hongzhao and other great ministers, then sent men to kill Taizu and Jun. Jun and the rest joined Taizu and marched on the capital.

sentences.zh: 太祖監國，以漢太后命拜峻樞密使。

translations.literal: Taizu supervised the state; by the Han Empress Dowager’s order he appointed Jun Privy Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu governed as regent and, by the Empress Dowager’s order, made Jun Privy Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 太祖將兵北出，至澶州，返軍向京師。

translations.literal: Taizu led troops north, reached Cang prefecture, then turned the army toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu marched north to Cang, then wheeled the army back on the capital.

sentences.zh: 是時，太祖已遣馮道迎湘陰公赟於徐州，而漢宗室蔡王信在許州。

translations.literal: At that time Taizu had already sent Feng Dao to welcome the Prince of Xiangyin Yun from Xuzhou, while the Han imperial clansman Prince of Cai Xin was at Xu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had already sent Feng Dao to meet the Prince of Xiangyin Yun at Xuzhou, while Prince of Cai Xin of the Han house held Xu.

sentences.zh: 峻與王殷謀，遣侍衛馬軍指揮使郭崇率兵之宋州、前申州刺史馬鐸之許州以伺變，崇、鐸遂幽赟而殺信。

translations.literal: Jun plotted with Wang Yin and sent Palace Cavalry commander Guo Chong with troops to Song prefecture and former Shen prefect Ma Duo to Xu to watch for trouble; Chong and Duo then detained Yun and killed Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Wang Yin sent Guo Chong’s horse to Song and Ma Duo, once prefect of Shen, to Xu to watch for shifts. Chong and Duo seized Yun and killed Xin.

sentences.zh: 太祖入立，拜峻右僕射、門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事，監修國史。

translations.literal: When Taizu entered and took the throne, he appointed Jun Right Vice Director, Gate Department Attendant-in-Chief, and Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and charged him with supervising the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu took the throne and made Jun Right Vice Director, Gate Attendant-in-Chief, Associate Grand Councilor, and supervisor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 劉旻攻晉州，峻為行營都部署，得以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Liu Min attacked Jin prefecture; Jun was made field-camp supreme commander and could act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Min attacked Jin. Jun was made field supreme commander with discretionary power.

sentences.zh: 別遣陳思讓、康延沼自烏嶺出絳州與峻會。

translations.literal: Separately he sent Chen Sirang and Kang Yanzhang out from Wuling toward Jiang prefecture to join Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Chen Sirang and Kang Yanzhang from Wuling toward Jiang to meet Jun.

sentences.zh: 峻至陜州，留不進。

translations.literal: Jun reached Shan prefecture and halted without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Jun reached Shan and stopped.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣使者翟守素馳至陜州，諭峻欲親征。

translations.literal: Taizu sent the envoy Zhai Shousu galloping to Shan to tell Jun he wished to campaign in person.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent Zhai Shousu racing to Shan to say he meant to take the field himself.

sentences.zh: 峻屏左右謂守素曰：「晉州城堅不可近，而劉旻兵銳亦未可當，臣所以留此者，非怯也，蓋有待爾。

translations.literal: Jun dismissed those beside him and told Shousu: "Jinzhou’s walls are firm and cannot be approached, and Liu Min’s troops are sharp and also cannot be faced. The reason your subject stays here is not cowardice—there is simply something to wait for.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent attendants away and told Shousu: "Jin’s walls cannot be neared and Liu Min’s men are too sharp to meet head-on. I stay here not from fear but because something must ripen first.

sentences.zh: 且陛下新即位，四方藩鎮，未有威德以加之，豈宜輕舉！

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty has newly taken the throne; the four quarters’ military commissioners still lack awe and virtue laid upon them—how could one move lightly!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is new on the throne; the border lords still lack awe of you—how can you stir lightly?

sentences.zh: 而兗州慕容彥超反跡已露，若陛下出汜水，則彥超入京師，陛下何以待之？

translations.literal: Yet Yan prefecture’s Murong Yanchao’s rebellious signs are already plain. If Your Majesty goes out by the Si River ford, Yanchao will enter the capital—how will Your Majesty meet that?
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao at Yan already shows rebellion. If you cross the Si ford, he will enter the capital—then what?

sentences.zh: 」守素馳還，具道峻言。

translations.literal: " Shousu galloped back and reported Jun’s words in full.
translations.idiomatic: " Shousu raced back and repeated Jun’s every word.

sentences.zh: 是時，太祖已下詔西幸，聞峻語，遽自提其耳曰：「幾敗吾事！

translations.literal: At that time Taizu had already issued an edict to tour west; hearing Jun’s words, he suddenly seized his own ear and said: "I nearly ruined my affair!
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had already ordered a western tour. Hearing Jun, he clutched his ear and cried: "I nearly wrecked everything!

sentences.zh: 」乃止不行。

translations.literal: " With that he halted and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: With that he called off the march.

sentences.zh: 峻軍出自絳州，前鋒報過蒙坑，峻喜，謂其屬曰：「蒙坑，晉、絳之險也，旻不分兵扼之，使吾過此，可知其必敗也。

translations.literal: Jun’s army came out from Jiang prefecture; the vanguard reported they had passed Mengkeng. Jun rejoiced and told his followers: "Mengkeng is the peril of Jin and Jiang. Min did not divide troops to hold it and let us pass—one can know he is sure to be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Jun’s army marched from Jiang. The van reported Mengkeng passed. Jun rejoiced and told his men: "Mengkeng is Jin and Jiang’s choke point. Min left it open—he is already beaten.

sentences.zh: 」峻軍去晉州一舍，旻聞周兵大至，即解去。

translations.literal: " Jun’s army was one stage from Jin prefecture when Min heard Zhou troops had come in force and at once lifted the siege and left.
translations.idiomatic: " A stage short of Jin, Min heard Zhou masses were coming and broke camp at once.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆欲追之，峻猶豫不決。

translations.literal: The generals all wished to pursue; Jun hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Every general wanted pursuit; Jun wavered.

sentences.zh: 明日，遣騎兵追旻，不及而還。

translations.literal: The next day he sent cavalry to pursue Min, failed to overtake him, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he sent horse after Min, could not catch him, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 從討慕容彥超，為隨駕都部署，率眾先登。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Murong Yanchao he was made Follow-the-Emperor Supreme Commander, leading the masses to mount first.
translations.idiomatic: Against Murong Yanchao he was Follow-the-Emperor supreme commander and took the walls first.

sentences.zh: 峻與太祖俱起於魏，自謂佐命之功，以天下為己任。

translations.literal: Jun and Taizu had both risen from Wei; he took his merit in aiding the mandate as his own and bore the realm as his charge.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Taizu had risen together from Wei. He counted his founding merit as his due and shouldered the realm.

sentences.zh: 凡所論請，事無大小，期於必得，或小不如誌，言色輒不遜，太祖每優容之。

translations.literal: Whatever he petitioned, great or small, he expected to obtain; if it fell slightly short of his wish, his words and bearing at once turned insubordinate, yet Taizu always indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: Every petition, large or small, had to succeed; the slightest miss turned his tone rude, yet Taizu indulged him.

sentences.zh: 峻年長於太祖二歲，往往呼峻為兄，或稱其字，峻由是益橫。

translations.literal: Jun was two years older than Taizu; Taizu often called Jun elder brother or used his style name, and Jun thereby grew all the more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was two years Taizu’s senior. Taizu often called him elder brother or used his style, and Jun grew bolder still.

sentences.zh: 鄭仁誨、李重進、向訓等，皆太祖故時偏裨，太祖初即位，謙抑未欲進用，而峻心忌之。

translations.literal: Zheng Renhui, Li Chongjin, Xiang Xun, and others were all Taizu’s old subordinate officers. When Taizu first took the throne he was modest and did not yet wish to advance them, and Jun inwardly resented them.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Renhui, Li Chongjin, and Xiang Xun had been Taizu’s old officers. At first he held them back, and Jun resented them.

sentences.zh: 自破慕容彥超還，即求解樞密以探上意，太祖慰勞之。

translations.literal: After returning from defeating Murong Yanchao he at once asked to be relieved of the Privy Commission to probe the emperor’s mind; Taizu comforted and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Back from breaking Yanchao he asked to quit the Privy Commission to test the throne; Taizu soothed him.

sentences.zh: 峻多發書諸鎮，求為保薦，居數日，諸鎮皆馳騎上峻書，太祖大駭。

translations.literal: Jun sent many letters to the various circuits seeking recommendations; within several days every circuit sent riders posting letters for Jun, and Taizu was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Jun flooded the circuits with letters seeking endorsements. Within days every circuit raced in with letters for him, and Taizu was shaken.

sentences.zh: 峻連章求解，因不視事，太祖遣近臣召之曰：「卿若不出，吾當自往候卿。

translations.literal: Jun submitted memorial after memorial asking to be relieved and therefore did not attend to affairs. Taizu sent a close attendant to summon him, saying: "If you will not come out, I shall go myself to wait on you.
translations.idiomatic: Jun memorialized again and again to resign and stopped attending court. Taizu sent a close man: "If you stay in, I will come wait on you myself.

sentences.zh: 」峻曰：「車駕若來，是致臣有不測也。

translations.literal: " Jun said: "If the imperial carriage comes, that is to bring your subject to misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: " Jun said: "If the carriage comes, you doom your servant.

sentences.zh: 」然殊無出意。

translations.literal: " Yet he showed no intent to come out.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet he would not budge.

sentences.zh: 樞密直學士陳同與峻相善，太祖即遣同召峻。

translations.literal: Privy Academy academician Chen Tong was on good terms with Jun; Taizu at once sent Tong to summon Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Privy academician Chen Tong was Jun’s friend; Taizu sent Tong to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 同還奏曰：「峻意少解，然請陛下聲言嚴駕，若將幸之，則峻必出矣。

translations.literal: Tong returned and reported: "Jun’s mood has eased somewhat, but he asks Your Majesty to proclaim a stern procession as if about to visit him—then Jun will surely come out.
translations.idiomatic: Tong reported: "Jun has softened a little, but ask Your Majesty to proclaim a stern procession as if you will visit—then he will come.

sentences.zh: 」太祖僶俛從之。

translations.literal: " Taizu bowed his head and followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizu yielded and did it.

sentences.zh: 峻聞太祖且來，遂馳入謁。

translations.literal: Jun heard Taizu was about to come and at once galloped in to audience.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Taizu was coming, Jun raced in to audience.

sentences.zh: 峻於樞密院起廳事，極其華侈，邀太祖臨幸，賜予甚厚。

translations.literal: Jun raised a reception hall at the Privy Council, making it extremely lavish, invited Taizu to visit, and bestowed gifts very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Jun built a reception hall at the Privy Council, lavish beyond measure, invited Taizu, and heaped gifts on him.

sentences.zh: 太祖於內園起一小殿，峻輒奏曰：「宮室已多，何用此為？

translations.literal: Taizu raised a small hall in the inner garden; Jun at once memorialized: "Palace chambers are already many—what use is this?
translations.idiomatic: Taizu built a small hall in the inner garden. Jun memorialized: "You already have halls enough—why this?

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「樞密院屋不少，卿亦何必有作？

translations.literal: " Taizu said: "The Privy Council has no few rooms either—why must you build?
translations.idiomatic: " Taizu said: "Your Privy Council is not short of rooms—why must you build?

sentences.zh: 」峻慚不能對。

translations.literal: " Jun was ashamed and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Jun flushed and had no answer.

sentences.zh: 峻為樞密使兼宰相，又求兼領平盧。

translations.literal: Jun was Privy Commissioner and also Grand Councilor, and further asked to hold Pinglu concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was Privy Commissioner and Grand Councilor and asked to hold Pinglu as well.

sentences.zh: 已受命，暫之鎮，又請借左藏庫綾萬匹，太祖皆勉從之。

translations.literal: Once he had received the appointment he went temporarily to his post, and again asked to borrow ten thousand bolts of silk from the Left Treasury; Taizu reluctantly granted all.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioned, he went briefly to his post and asked ten thousand bolts of silk from the Left Treasury; Taizu grudgingly agreed to all.

sentences.zh: 又請用顏衎、陳同代李谷、範質為相，太祖曰：「進退宰相，豈可倉卒？

translations.literal: He again asked to use Yan Kan and Chen Tong in place of Li Gu and Fan Zhi as chancellors. Taizu said: "Advancing and retiring chancellors—how can that be rushed?
translations.idiomatic: He asked Yan Kan and Chen Tong to replace Li Gu and Fan Zhi. Taizu said: "Chancellors are not swapped in haste.

sentences.zh: 當徐思之。

translations.literal: We should consider it slowly.
translations.idiomatic: I will think on it.

sentences.zh: 」峻論請不已，語漸不遜。

translations.literal: " Jun’s petitions and arguments did not cease, and his words gradually turned insubordinate.
translations.idiomatic: " Jun would not stop pressing, and his tone turned rude.

sentences.zh: 日亭午，太祖未食，峻爭不已，是時寒食假，太祖曰：「俟假開，當為卿行。

translations.literal: The sun stood at noon and Taizu had not eaten; Jun argued without end. It was then the Cold Food holiday, and Taizu said: "Wait until the holiday ends—I will act for you.
translations.idiomatic: Noon came and Taizu had not eaten while Jun argued on. It was Cold Food; Taizu said: "When the holiday ends I will do as you ask.

sentences.zh: 」峻乃退。

translations.literal: " Jun then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Jun withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太祖遂不能忍，明日禦便殿，召百官皆入，即幽峻於別所。

translations.literal: Taizu could bear it no longer. The next day he held court in the informal hall, summoned all officials to enter, and at once confined Jun in a separate place.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu could bear no more. Next day at the informal hall he called every official in and locked Jun away apart.

sentences.zh: 太祖見馮道，泣曰：「峻淩朕，不能忍！

translations.literal: Taizu saw Feng Dao and wept, saying: "Jun bullies me—I cannot bear it!
translations.idiomatic: Taizu saw Feng Dao in tears: "Jun rides over me—I cannot endure it!

sentences.zh: 」即貶商州司馬，卒於貶所。

translations.literal: " He was at once demoted to Shang prefecture marshal and died in exile.
translations.idiomatic: " He was demoted to Shang marshal at once and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 峻已被黜，太祖以峻監修國史，意其所書不實，因召史官取日曆讀之，史官以禁中事非外所知，懼以漏落得罪。

translations.literal: After Jun had been removed, Taizu, because Jun had supervised the national history, suspected what he wrote was untrue and therefore summoned the historians to fetch the daily calendar and read it. The historians, since inner-palace affairs were not known outside, feared they would be punished for omissions.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was gone, but he had supervised the history. Taizu feared the record was false and called historians to read the daily calendar. They feared palace matters they did not know would cost them for gaps.

sentences.zh: 峻貶後，李穀監修，因請命近臣錄禁中事付史館，乃命樞密直學士就樞密院錄送史館，自此始。

translations.literal: After Jun’s demotion Li Gu supervised the compilation and therefore asked that close officials record inner-palace affairs and deliver them to the History Office; Taizu then ordered Privy Academy academics to record at the Privy Council and send copies to the History Office—from this it began.
translations.idiomatic: After Jun’s fall Li Gu supervised the history and asked close officials to log palace affairs for the History Office. Taizu ordered Privy academics to record at the council and send copies to the History Office—thus it began.

sentences.zh: 王殷，大名人也。

translations.literal: Wang Yin was a native of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin came from Daming.

sentences.zh: 少為軍卒，以軍功累遷靈武馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: In youth he was a soldier; by military merit he was repeatedly promoted to Lingwu horse-and-foot commander.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was a soldier and rose by merit to Lingwu horse-and-foot commander.

sentences.zh: 唐廢帝時，從範延光討張令昭於魏，以功拜祁州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Tang’s Deposed Emperor he followed Fan Yanguang in campaigning against Zhang Lingzhao at Wei and, by merit, was made prefect of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Deposed Emperor he followed Fan Yanguang against Zhang Lingzhao at Wei and was made prefect of Qi.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，徙原州刺史。

translations.literal: In Jin’s Tianfu era he was transferred to Yuan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin Tianfu he was moved to Yuan.

sentences.zh: 殷事母以孝聞，欲與人遊，必先白母，母所不可者，未嘗取往。

translations.literal: Yin was famed for filial service to his mother. When he wished to go out with others he always told his mother first; what his mother did not permit he never went to do.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was known for honoring his mother. Before any outing he asked her leave; what she forbade he never did.

sentences.zh: 及為刺史，政事有小失，母責之，殷即取杖授婢仆，自笞於母前。

translations.literal: When he became prefect, if there was some small fault in government his mother reproved him; Yin at once took a staff, handed it to maidservants, and flogged himself before his mother.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect, small slips drew his mother’s scolding. He handed a staff to servants and whipped himself before her.

sentences.zh: 母亡服喪，晉高祖詔殷起復，以為憲州刺史，殷乞終喪。

translations.literal: When his mother died he wore mourning; Jin Gaozu ordered Yin to resume office and made him prefect of Xian, but Yin begged to finish mourning.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died and he mourned. Jin Gaozu ordered him back to office as Xian prefect; Yin begged to finish mourning.

sentences.zh: 服除，出帝以為奉國右廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: When mourning ended the Deposed Emperor made him commander of the Right Flank of the Nation-Supporting army.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning done, the Deposed Emperor made him Right Flank commander of Nation-Supporting.

sentences.zh: 後從漢高祖討杜重威，先登力戰，矢中其腦，鏃自口出而不死，高祖嘉之，以為侍衛步軍都指揮使，領寧江軍節度使。

translations.literal: Later he followed Han Gaozu in campaigning against Du Chongwei, mounting first and fighting with force; an arrow struck his brain and the point came out through his mouth, yet he did not die. Gaozu praised him and made him Palace Foot Guard commander, holding the Ningjiang military commission.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Han Gaozu against Du Chongwei, climbed first, and fought hard. An arrow struck his brain and the head came out his mouth, yet he lived. Gaozu praised him and made him Palace Foot Guard commander with Ningjiang.

sentences.zh: 契丹犯邊，漢遣殷以兵屯澶州。

translations.literal: When the Khitan raided the border, Han sent Yin with troops to garrison at Cang.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan raids brought Yin with troops to Cang.

sentences.zh: 隱帝已殺楊邠等，詔鎮寧軍節度使李弘義殺殷於澶州，又詔郭崇殺周太祖於魏。

translations.literal: The Hidden Emperor had already killed Yang Bin and others; he ordered Zhenning military commissioner Li Hongyi to kill Yin at Cang, and also ordered Guo Chong to kill Zhou Taizu at Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Hidden Emperor had killed Yang Bin and others and ordered Li Hongyi to kill Yin at Cang and Guo Chong to kill Taizu at Wei.

sentences.zh: 詔書至澶州，弘義恐事不果，反以告殷，殷遣人馳至魏告周太祖，遂起兵反。

translations.literal: When the edict reached Cang, Hongyi feared the affair would fail and instead told Yin. Yin sent a man galloping to Wei to inform Zhou Taizu, and they then raised troops in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: The edict reached Cang. Hongyi feared failure and warned Yin. Yin sent a rider to Wei; Taizu rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 太祖入立，拜侍衛親軍都指揮使，出為天雄軍節度使、同中書門下平章事，仍領親軍，自河以北皆受殷節度。

translations.literal: When Taizu entered and took the throne he appointed Yin Palace Personal Guard commander, sent him out as Tianxiong military commissioner and Associate Grand Councilor, and still had him lead the Personal Guard; north of the river all obeyed Yin’s command.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu took the throne and made Yin Personal Guard commander and Tianxiong commissioner and Associate Grand Councilor, still leading the guard. All north of the river answered to Yin.

sentences.zh: 殷頗務聚斂，太祖聞而惡之，遣人謂之曰：「吾起魏時，帑廩儲畜豈少邪？

translations.literal: Yin was quite given to amassing wealth. Taizu heard of it and detested him, sending someone to say: "When I rose from Wei, were the treasury stores few?
translations.idiomatic: Yin amassed wealth. Taizu hated it and sent word: "When I rose from Wei, were the vaults empty?

sentences.zh: 汝為國家用，足矣。

translations.literal: Use enough for the state—that suffices.
translations.idiomatic: Take enough for the state—that is plenty.

sentences.zh: 」殷不聽。

translations.literal: " Yin would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " Yin would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 殷與王峻俱從太祖起自魏，後峻得罪，殷不自安。

translations.literal: Yin and Wang Jun had both followed Taizu in rising from Wei. After Jun fell from grace Yin was ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and Wang Jun had risen with Taizu from Wei. After Jun’s fall Yin could not rest easy.

sentences.zh: 廣順三年秋九月永壽節，殷求入為壽，太祖許之，而懼其疑也，復遣使止之。

translations.literal: In autumn, ninth month, the Yongshou festival of the third year of Guangshun, Yin asked to enter court for the birthday rites; Taizu permitted it, yet fearing his suspicion, again sent an envoy to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, ninth month, Yongshou of Guangshun year three, Yin asked to come for birthday rites. Taizu agreed, then feared his mind and sent men to turn him back.

sentences.zh: 明年，太祖有事於南郊。

translations.literal: The next year Taizu had business at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Taizu sacrificed at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 是冬，殷來朝，殷握兵柄，職當警衛，出入多以兵從，又求兵甲，以備非常。

translations.literal: That winter Yin came to court. Yin held military power; his duty was to guard, yet going in and out he mostly took troops with him, and he also asked for arms and armor against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Yin came to court. He held the armies, should have guarded the palace, yet marched with troops and asked arms against trouble.

sentences.zh: 是時，太祖臥疾，疑殷有異志，乃力疾禦滋德殿，殷入起居，即命執之，削奪在身官爵，長流登州。

translations.literal: At that time Taizu lay ill and suspected Yin of ulterior intent. He forced himself to hold court at Zide Hall; when Yin entered for the daily greeting he at once ordered him seized, stripped every office and rank he still held, and exiled him far to Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu lay ill and suspected Yin. He dragged himself to Zide Hall; Yin came to greet him and was seized at once, stripped of rank, and exiled to Deng.

sentences.zh: 已而殺之，徙其家屬於登州。

translations.literal: Before long he was killed, and his household was moved to Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was killed and his family sent to Deng.

sentences.zh: 劉詞，字好謙，大名元城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Ci, style Haoqian, was a native of Yuancheng in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ci, styled Haoqian, came from Yuancheng in Daming.

sentences.zh: 少事楊師厚，以勇悍知名。

translations.literal: In youth he served Yang Shihou and was famed for fierce daring.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served Yang Shihou and was known for fierce dash.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗下魏博，與梁戰夾河，詞以軍功為效節軍使，遷長劍指揮使，坐事左遷汝州十餘年。

translations.literal: When Tang’s Zhuangzong descended on Wei-Bo and fought Liang on the river, Ci by military merit became Loyalty Manifestation army commissioner, was promoted to Long-Sword commander, and by offense was demoted to Yu prefecture for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong took Wei-Bo and fought Liang on the river. Ci rose to Loyalty Manifestation commissioner and Long-Sword commander, then sat ten-odd years demoted at Yu.

sentences.zh: 廢帝時，詔諸州鎮選驍勇者充禁軍，詞得選為禁軍校。

translations.literal: Under the Deposed Emperor an edict ordered the various prefectures and commissions to select fierce brave men to fill the Palace Guard; Ci was selected as a Palace Guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor ordered circuits to pick the fierce for the Palace Guard; Ci was chosen.

sentences.zh: 從破張從賓、楊光遠，以功遷奉國第一軍都虞候。

translations.literal: He followed in defeating Zhang Congbin and Yang Guangyuan and, by merit, was promoted to Nation-Supporting First Army deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: He helped break Zhang Congbin and Yang Guangyuan and rose to Nation-Supporting First Army deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 從馬全節破安州，以功遷指揮使。

translations.literal: He followed Ma Quanjie in defeating An prefecture and, by merit, was promoted to commander.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Ma Quanjie at An and rose to commander.

sentences.zh: 從杜重威破鎮州，以先登功拜泌州刺史。

translations.literal: He followed Du Chongwei in defeating Zhen prefecture and, by the merit of mounting first, was made prefect of Bi.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Du Chongwei at Zhen, climbed first, and was made prefect of Bi.

sentences.zh: 晉軍討安從進，為襄州行營都虞候，以功遷泌州團練使。

translations.literal: When Jin troops campaigned against An Congjin he was Xiang prefecture field-camp deputy commander and, by merit, was promoted to Bi training commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Jin marched on An Congjin. He was Xiang field deputy commander and rose to Bi training commissioner.

sentences.zh: 徙房州，歲餘，為政不苛撓，人頗便之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Fang prefecture; after more than a year his government was not harsh or troubling, and the people found it quite convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Fang. A year on, his rule was light and the people were at ease.

sentences.zh: 詞居暇日，常被甲枕戈而臥，謂人曰：「我以此取富貴，豈可一日輒忘之？

translations.literal: On his free days Ci often wore armor and slept with a weapon for a pillow, telling others: "I won wealth and honor by this—how could I forget it for a single day!
translations.idiomatic: On free days Ci slept in mail with a blade for pillow and told others: "I won rank by this—how forget it for one day!

sentences.zh: 且人情易習，若一墮其筋力，有事何以報國！

translations.literal: Moreover human hearts are quick to grow accustomed; if one falls once from his sinews and strength, when trouble comes how will he repay the state!
translations.idiomatic: Hearts grow soft in ease. Let muscle fail once and how will you serve the state when trouble comes?

sentences.zh: 」漢高祖時，復為奉國右廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: " Under Han Gaozu he again became Nation-Supporting Right Flank commander.
translations.idiomatic: " Under Han Gaozu he again commanded Nation-Supporting Right Flank.

sentences.zh: 漢軍討李守貞於河中，詞以侍衛步軍都指揮使領寧江軍節度使，為行營都虞候，以功拜鎮國軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Han troops campaigned against Li Shouzhen at Hezhong, Ci as Palace Foot Guard commander holding the Ningjiang commission was field-camp deputy commander and, by merit, was made Zhenguo military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Han marched on Li Shouzhen at Hezhong. Ci was Foot Guard commander with Ningjiang and field deputy commander, then Zhenguo commissioner by merit.

sentences.zh: 周太祖入立，加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu entered and took the throne he was further made Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu took the throne and added Associate Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 歷鎮安國、河陽三城。

translations.literal: He successively held Anguo, Heyang, and the Three Cities.
translations.idiomatic: He held Anguo, Heyang, and the Three Cities in turn.

sentences.zh: 世宗戰高平，樊愛能等軍敗南走，遇詞而止之曰：「軍敗矣，可無前也。

translations.literal: At Shizong’s Gaoping battle, Fan Aineng and the others’ armies were defeated and fled south. Meeting Ci they stopped him and said: "The army is beaten—you need not go forward.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaoping, Fan Aineng’s men broke south. They met Ci and cried: "The army is lost—go no farther.

sentences.zh: 」詞不聽，輒趣兵以進，世宗嘉之，以為隨駕都部署。

translations.literal: " Ci would not listen and at once urged his troops forward. Shizong praised him and made him Follow-the-Emperor Supreme Commander.
translations.idiomatic: " Ci would not hear them and drove his men on. Shizong praised him and made him Follow-the-Emperor supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 及班師，以為河東行營副都部署，徙鎮永興。

translations.literal: When the army returned from campaign he was made Hedong field-camp deputy supreme commander and transferred to hold Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was Hedong field deputy supreme commander, then transferred to Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 明年卒於鎮，年六十五，贈侍中，謚忠惠。

translations.literal: The next year he died in post, age sixty-five; posthumously he was made Palace Attendant and given the posthumous title Loyal and Kind.
translations.idiomatic: He died in post next year at sixty-five, posthumously Palace Attendant with the title Loyal and Kind.

sentences.zh: 初，昶遣其秦州節度使高處儔以兵援環，未至，聞堂倉兵敗，亦潰歸，處儔判官趙比閉城不內，處儔遂奔成都，比乃以城降，成、階二州相繼亦降，獨環堅守百餘日，然後克之。

translations.literal: At first Chang sent his Qin prefecture military commissioner Gao Chuchou with troops to aid Huan. Before he arrived he heard the Tangcang army had been defeated and also fled in rout. Chuchou’s aide Zhao Bi closed the city and would not admit him; Chuchou then fled to Chengdu, and Bi thereupon surrendered the city. Cheng and Jie prefectures in succession also surrendered; only Huan held firm more than a hundred days, and then it was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Chang sent Gao Chuchou from Qin to aid Huan. Chuchou heard Tangcang had fallen and fled. His aide Zhao Bi shut him out; Chuchou ran to Chengdu and Bi surrendered. Cheng and Jie followed; only Huan held a hundred-odd days before the city fell.

sentences.zh: 世宗召見環，嘆曰：「三州已降，環獨堅守，吾數以書招之，而環不答，至於力屈就擒，雖不能死，亦忠其所事也，用之可勸事君者。

translations.literal: Shizong summoned Huan to audience and sighed: "The three prefectures have surrendered; Huan alone held firm. I several times wrote to summon him, yet Huan did not answer. When his strength was spent he was taken—though he could not die, he was loyal to whom he served. Employing him can encourage those who serve their lords.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong called Huan in and sighed: "Three prefectures yielded; Huan alone held. I wrote again and again; he never answered. Broken, he was taken—he could not die, yet he was loyal. Use him to teach service.

sentences.zh: 」乃拜環右驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: " He then appointed Huan Right Valiant Cavalry general.
translations.idiomatic: " He made Huan Right Valiant Cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 是時，周師已征淮，即以環佐侯章為攻取賊城水砦副部署。

translations.literal: At that time Zhou troops had already campaigned on the Huai, and Huan was at once made assistant to Hou Zhang as deputy commander for taking the rebels’ river forts and water stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was already on the Huai. Huan was made Hou Zhang’s deputy for seizing rebel river forts.

sentences.zh: 初，周師南征，李景陳兵於淮，舟楫甚盛，周師無水戰之具，世宗患之，乃置造船務於京城之西，為戰艦數百艘，得景降卒，教之水戰。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhou troops campaigned south, Li Jing arrayed troops on the Huai and his boats and oars were very grand; Zhou troops lacked gear for river fighting. Shizong was troubled by this and therefore established a shipbuilding office west of the capital, built several hundred warships, took Jing’s surrendered soldiers, and had them teach river combat.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou first marched south, Li Jing massed boats on the Huai. Zhou had no river gear. Shizong founded a shipyard west of the capital, built hundreds of warships, and had Jing’s surrendered men teach river war.

sentences.zh: 明年，世宗再征淮，使環將水戰卒數千，自蔡河以入淮。

translations.literal: The next year Shizong campaigned on the Huai again and had Huan lead several thousand river-combat troops, entering the Huai from the Cai River.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Shizong marched on the Huai again and sent Huan with thousands of river troops in from the Cai.

sentences.zh: 環居軍中，未嘗有戰功。

translations.literal: Huan dwelt in the army yet never had battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: Huan served in the ranks but never won battle merit.

sentences.zh: 蜀卒與環俱擒者，世宗不殺，悉以從軍，後多南奔於景，世宗待環益不疑。

translations.literal: Among the Shu soldiers captured together with Huan, Shizong did not kill them but all took them into the army. Later many fled south to Jing, yet Shizong treated Huan all the more without suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Shu men captured with Huan Shizong spared and kept in the ranks. Many later fled south to Jing, yet Shizong trusted Huan all the more.

sentences.zh: 已而景將許文縝、邊鎬等皆被擒，世宗悉以為將軍，與環等列第京師，歲時賜與甚厚。

translations.literal: Before long Li Jing’s generals Xu Wenzhen, Bian Hao, and the rest were all captured; Shizong made them all generals, housed them with Huan and the others in estates at the capital, and gave them generous seasonal gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Jing’s generals Xu Wenzhen, Bian Hao, and the rest were taken. Shizong made them all generals, lodged them with Huan and the others in capital estates, and lavished seasonal gifts on them.

sentences.zh: 明年又幸淮南，又以環從，遇疾，卒於泗州。

translations.literal: The next year Shizong again went on campaign to Huainan and again had Huan follow; he fell ill and died at Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Shizong marched on Huainan again with Huan in his train; he fell ill and died at Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 折從阮

translations.literal: Zhe Congruan
translations.idiomatic: Zhe Congruan

sentences.zh: 折從阮，字可久，初名從遠，避漢高祖名，改為阮，雲中人也。

translations.literal: Zhe Congruan, styled Kejiu, was at first named Congyuan; to avoid Han Gaozu’s taboo name he changed it to Ruan. He was a native of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe Congruan, styled Kejiu, was first named Congyuan; to avoid Han Gaozu’s taboo he took the name Ruan. He came from Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 其父嗣倫，為麟州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Silun was prefect of Lin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Silun was prefect of Lin.

sentences.zh: 從阮為人，溫恭長者，居父喪，以孝聞。

translations.literal: Congruan was by nature a warm, respectful elder; in mourning his father he was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Congruan was a warm, respectful elder by nature; mourning his father, he was known for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗鎮太原，以為牙將，後以為府州刺史。

translations.literal: When Tang Zhuangzong held Taiyuan, Congruan was made a tooth officer; later he was made prefect of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong held Taiyuan, Congruan was made a tooth officer; later he was made prefect of Fu.

sentences.zh: 晉出帝與契丹敗盟，從阮以兵攻契丹，取其城堡十餘，遷本州團練使，兼領朔州刺史、安北都護、振武軍節度使、契丹西南面行營馬步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: When Jin’s Last Emperor broke alliance with the Khitan, Congruan attacked the Khitan with troops, took more than ten of their forts, was moved to regimental trainer of his prefecture, and concurrently held prefect of Shuo, Defender-General of the North, military commissioner of the Zhenwu army, and army inspector of the Khitan Southwestern Army infantry and cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin’s Last Emperor broke with the Khitan, Congruan struck them and took a dozen forts. He was made regimental trainer of his prefecture and concurrently prefect of Shuo, Defender-General of the North, Zhenwu commissioner, and army inspector of the Khitan Southwestern Army horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖入立，於府州建永安軍，以從阮為節度使。

translations.literal: When Han Gaozu took the throne, he established the Yong’an army at Fu and made Congruan its military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Gaozu took the throne, he founded the Yong’an army at Fu and made Congruan its commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年，以其族朝京師，徙鎮武勝，即拜從阮子德扆為府州團練使。

translations.literal: The next year he brought his clan to court at the capital, was moved to Wusheng, and Congruan’s son De Yi was at once made regimental trainer of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he brought his clan to court, was moved to Wusheng, and his son De Yi was at once made regimental trainer of Fu.

sentences.zh: 周太祖入立，從阮歷徙宣義、保義、靜難三鎮。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu took the throne, Congruan was transferred in succession through the three circuits Xuanyi, Baoyi, and Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, Congruan was moved in turn through Xuanyi, Baoyi, and Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 顯德二年，罷還京師，行至洛陽卒，贈中書令。

translations.literal: In Xiande year 2 he was dismissed and returned to the capital; he died en route at Luoyang and was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiande year 2 he was recalled to the capital; he died on the road at Luoyang and was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat.
